newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: The Argentine bolsa closed lower on Wednesday on profit-taking after its blue chip index MerVal reached Tuesday a year-high of 640.44 points.
"In a certain way profit-takings were normal considering the strong business activity seen on Tuesday," said Dario Lizzano, analyst for Banco Santander.
"There are institutional investors awating to get new bargains. There will be some downward corrections but the market's health for the medium termn is still sound."
The MerVal shed 1.08 percent to close at 628.76 points after having risen 13.6 percent in the last five weeks.
A decline in the Dow Jones matched by Argentine ADRs and bonds prompted sales in the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.

Nevertheless, a strong decline in volume to $23.4 million from Tuesday's $40 million shows most investors are reluctant to sell in the face of the sound outlook for the market. Local stock and bond prices are set to rise in the medium term due to signs of domestic economic recovery, analysts said.
The Merval has a resistance level of 650 points and a support level around 600, a stock broker said.
Losers beat gainers 41 to 14 with 16 issues flat.
Biggest losses among main tiers were food giant Molinos and oil company ASTRA with 3.22 and 2.68 percent falls respectively.
Investors are eyeing the release of U.S. unemployment data Friday to see whether it would impact U.S. bonds and consequently on liquidity flows to emerging markets.
